summary: Intermittent handoff to remote PoP causing connection retries and inference p99 spike for enterprise customer
description:
Issue summary:
NimbusApps reported elevated inference tail latency (p99 > 3s) and a spike in client-side connection retries observed between 2026-03-13T09:30Z and 2026-03-13T11:15Z. Errors manifest as streaming disconnects and repeat requests with 504 timeouts.

Impact:
- A subset (~6%) of NimbusApps production traffic experienced repeated request retries and session reconnects, increasing token costs and user-visible latency.
- Affects their real-time chat feature powered by text-generation-2.1 and fallback rwl-13b-q4.

Environment:
- Customer workspace: NimbusApps (Enterprise) on Redwood hosted API
- Regions observed: primary customer traffic originates in ap-southeast-1; some requests elevated to us-east-1 PoP during the window.
- Config: model pinned to text-generation-2.1; streaming enabled; account-level region affinity configured but not strict.

Steps to reproduce (how customer observed):
1) Send a streaming generation request from ap-southeast-1 with long prefix (~600 tokens) at 50 RPS.
2) After ~2–3 minutes, ~1/20 connections drop with client-side ECONNRESET and server-side TLS renegotiation logs.
3) Client retries immediately; a fraction of retries are routed to us-east-1 PoP, which returns slightly different model variant and triggers additional cold-kv misses.

Observed behavior:
- p50/p95 mostly stable; p99 jumps from ~400ms to 3–4s during handoffs.
- Logs show repeated TLS session renegotiation and unexpected SNAT source IP changes for the same account span.
- KV cache miss rate for prefix cache increases ~8x for affected requests.

Hypothesis / initial theory:
- An intermittent egress routing adjustment caused a small percentage of sessions to be handed off to a distant PoP (us-east-1). The handoff path performed a new TLS handshake and used a different SNAT, invalidating per-connection cache affinity and causing cold KV/cache repopulation and higher model warmup latency.

Immediate mitigations applied:
- We enabled account-level strict-region-affinity for NimbusApps to force ap-southeast-1 serving while we investigate (applied 2026-03-13T10:02Z).
- Short-term circuit: increased streaming retry backoff to avoid rapid retries and token cost amplification (applied 2026-03-13T10:10Z).

Next steps / long-term actions:
- Engineering to review egress routing logs and PoP handoff traces to determine trigger for cross-region failover.
- Add telemetry to correlate SNAT changes with PoP selection and KV cache invalidation.
- Consider failover policy update: prefer local PoP for accounts with streaming affinity and long-prefix workloads.

Resolution plan status:
- Under investigation by SRE (assignee Evan Chen). We have a reproducible trace and temporary customer-side mitigation in place.

References and artifacts:
- Traces: https://observability.redwood.ai/trace/INC-2026-0313-07
- Dashboards: https://metrics.redwood.ai/d/edge-routing/po-phandoff-overview
- Slack thread: #support (thread ts: 2026-03-13T09:42Z)
comments: 2026-03-13 09:45 - Lucia Park: Customer reported p99 spike and streaming disconnects. They provided request IDs and a sample trace. Escalating to SRE.
2026-03-13 10:00 - SRE Triage: Initial review shows occasional handoff traces landing in us-east-1. Marking as P1 due to customer impact. Assigned to Evan Chen.
2026-03-13 10:05 - Evan Chen: Enabled strict-region-affinity for the customer to reduce cross-region handoffs. Requesting routing team logs for 09:20–11:30Z window.
2026-03-13 10:12 - Customer (NimbusApps engineer): Confirmed reduced retry volume after affinity change; still observing a small number of lingering 504s. Asking for ETA on permanent fix.
2026-03-13 11:00 - Evan Chen: Found correlated BGP withdraw/announce events from our transit peer during the window; opening investigation with networking. See linked PR and runbook.
2026-03-14 08:30 - Networking: Identified transient route flap on peer ASN 64512 that affected selective PoP egress. Working on BGP dampening and health-check gating for PoP handoff.
investigation_notes: Collected request ids: SUP-CUST-261409-{rids}. Initial trace shows session A (client IP X) received SYN to PoP ap-southeast-1, then a small percentage got retried and routed to us-east-1 PoP where TLS renegotiation occurred. KV prefix cache misses align with timestamps of SNAT IP change. Networking team flagged peer route flap. Hypothesis: transient transit event caused a subset of flows to re-evaluate path leading to PoP selection change; path change triggered new TLS session and cache invalidation. Next: correlate edge-proxy handoff logs with BGP updates and run replay test with controlled route withdraws.
resolution: Workaround and mitigation applied: enforced strict region affinity for NimbusApps and increased client-side retry backoff. Networking rolled BGP dampening and deployed health-check gating for PoP handoff at 2026-03-14T07:20Z. Pending: deployment of a config to prefer local PoP for streaming-heavy accounts in next release (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/482). Ticket will be updated when change is released and verified.
follow_up_items: 1) Add PoP-affinity telemetry in tracing to catch SNAT+PoP correlation (owner: SRE). 2) Update failover policy to respect streaming affinity for pinned model accounts (owner: Routing). 3) Postmortem and customer RCA to be published to Confluence by 2026-03-18.
